topic: Index admission cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
usual_baseline: Most units fall far short of cholecystectomy within 7–8 days: often 0–20% (0/61, 10%, 11%, 18.2%, 18.4%), a few 47–58.5%, and 75–87% in two. Waits after discharge run to months (68–125.8 days; 98.2 weeks). Readmission while waiting is common: 14–58%. Theatre capacity and ERCP/MRCP delays are the usual causes.
fix_that_works: A full pathway with more ultrasound, a weekly theatre session and senior-led coding: 58% to 100% within 8 days [2227]. An e-referral system: wait 98.2 to 47.7 weeks [2186]. A referral proforma: pathway acceptance 10.5% to 29.2%, stay 6.45 to 3.88 days [2520]. Median admission to theatre 106.5 to 70.7 hours [2467].
fix_that_fails: Teaching and posters: within 7 days 75.3% to 68% [2336]. A hot gallbladder list and weekend list during COVID: hot gallbladder rate 8.8% to 10.8%, readmission 20.6% to 29.7% [2309]. A weekly hot list gave only 14% compliance [2122]. Opening the hot list to other surgeons left overall surgery at 21% [2389].
consultant_advice: Overdone. Nearly every unit finds the same low rate and the same cause, theatre capacity. Don't repeat the timing audit. Measure readmissions and bed days while waiting, or coding accuracy (60% miscoded in one audit), to make the business case.
